title: Home-visit physiotherapy for frail osteoarthritis (UK)
meta_description: When home physiotherapy may be offered for frail people with osteoarthritis, what a visit involves, and how to keep up strength exercises between visits.

direct_answer: Physiotherapists may visit at home if you cannot easily attend a clinic, for example after a hospital stay or during reablement. Visits usually include an assessment, a tailored exercise plan and advice on walking aids. Keeping up exercises between visits helps.

content:
For people with osteoarthritis and frailty, getting to a clinic can be hard. Home visits may be available in some situations.

This guide explains what to expect. It is educational information, not a diagnosis or personal treatment plan.

When home visits may be offered

  • After a hospital stay.
  • As part of reablement or intermediate care.
  • If you are housebound.

What a visit involves

  • An assessment of movement, strength and balance.
  • A tailored exercise plan.
  • Advice on walking aids and safety.

Strength and steadiness exercises

  • Sit-to-stand from a chair.
  • Seated leg exercises.
  • Supported standing balance practice.
  • Build up gradually.

Between visits

Use a written or picture plan and a diary. Ask a family member to support you.

When to get help

  • Call 999 for chest pain, trouble breathing, signs of a stroke, or a fall with a possible serious injury.
  • Get urgent advice the same day (NHS 111 or your GP) for sudden confusion, a sudden drop in mobility, or a hot, swollen joint with fever.
  • See your GP for a steady decline over weeks, unplanned weight loss or repeated falls.

Never stop or change a prescribed medicine yourself. Ask your GP or pharmacist for a review.

Common questions

How do I get home physio?

Ask your GP or discharge team.

Is physio worth it with arthritis?

Exercise is a core treatment for osteoarthritis.

Sources and further reading

  • NICE NG74: Intermediate care including reablement
  • NHS: Strength exercises

Living With Arthritis is an independent charity and is not part of Arthritis UK (formerly Versus Arthritis). Everyone's situation is different, so follow the advice of your own GP and care team. If you feel very unwell, call 999 or go to A&E. For urgent advice, contact NHS 111 (NHS 24 on 111 in Scotland; in Northern Ireland, your GP or GP out-of-hours service).
